name: Regal
lede: Regal is a deep, slightly purple navy, with a name that usually points to purple.

sections.title: A royal word for a blue
sections.body:
Our name records first list this color in the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 [1]. Nothing in the color books we hold describes this specific swatch, so its origin is undocumented here [1]. The swatch itself is a dark blue with a trace of violet, not the red-leaning purple the word usually calls to mind [1].

The word, though, has a long history with purple. Gage notes that, in medieval color symbolism, the regal purple of Christ's robe may be the same as the scarlet of sin [2]. And in Gujarat, one Indian dye book describes a range of colors, from "regal purple" to the color of kidney beans, all made from indigo combinations [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive the color appears in 16 paintings, as photographed, rarer than 69% of the named colors [1]. The earliest in our set is by Bronzino, in 1543, centuries before the name's first record, so this is a look-alike hue, not a sign of the dye [1]. Related names: [[royal-purple]], [[midnight-blue]] and [[royal-blue]].
